name: Mmai
summary: 5-Methoxy-6-methyl-2-aminoindane (MMAI) is a drug of the 2-aminoindane family developed in the 1990s by a team led by David E. Nichols at Purdue University. It acts as a highly selective serotonin releasing agent (SSRA) with lower neurotoxicity than MDMA and produces entactogenic effects in humans. The drug has been sold as a designer drug online.

pharmacology.text: MMAI is one of the only known monoamine releasing agents with greater than 100-fold selectivity for the serotonin transporter (SERT) over the dopamine transporter (DAT). Receptor interaction data for MMAI have also been reported.

uses.text: The drug has been sold as a designer drug online.
